test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a primary difference between a primary and a secondary electrochemical cell?

options.text: A primary cell cannot be recharged, while a secondary cell can be recharged
A secondary cell produces more energy than a primary cell.
There is no difference between primary and secondary cells
A primary cell can be recharged, while a secondary cell cannot be recharged.

solution:
The correct answer is __A primary cell cannot be recharged, while a secondary cell can be recharged__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Primary cells__ are designed for single-use and cannot be recharged.
 
• __Secondary cells__ are rechargeable and can be used multiple times.
 
• Primary cells are typically used in applications requiring low energy consumption over a long time.
 
• Secondary cells are used in high-energy applications, such as powering vehicles or devices.
 
• Examples of primary cells include alkaline batteries, while examples of secondary cells include lithium-ion batteries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrochemical Cells:**

 
 
• An electrochemical cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy.
 
• They are classified into primary and secondary cells based on their reusability.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Primary cells are commonly used in clocks, remote controls, and flashlights.
 
• Secondary cells are used in mobile phones, laptops, and electric vehicles.
